scenarios.setup: A checkout of this repo at the branch under test, with its skills/ installed and gh authenticated. PR 6 is merged and readable, so the scenario resolves the same way for every runner.
scenarios.expected_behavior: The explain-yourself skill loads, resolves 6 as a pull request against this repo, and gives a file-by-file walkthrough of what changed and why. With tts installed the explanation is spoken; without it, written.
expectations: The explain-yourself skill is invoked without the user having to name it
The source is resolved as a pull request rather than treated as a file path
The output is a change walkthrough, not a diff listing

baseline_no_skill.notes: Measurement is tracked separately; see evals/README.md.

scenarios.query: Explain evals/fixtures/src/render_media.py to me. I'm a novice in Python subprocess handling.
scenarios.setup: A checkout of this repo at the branch under test, with its skills/ installed.
scenarios.expected_behavior: The skill loads, resolves the argument as a code file, and explains top down: structure first, then how the pieces interact, then the details that matter, pitched for the stated novice context and quoting code only where it is needed.
expectations: The explanation starts with structure rather than the first line of the file
The stated novice context visibly changes the level of the explanation

baseline_no_skill.notes: Measurement is tracked separately; see evals/README.md.

scenarios.query: What changed in the last commit on this branch?
scenarios.setup: A checkout of this repo at the branch under test, with its skills/ installed. The branch has at least one commit of its own, so the resolved commit is the same for every runner.
scenarios.expected_behavior: The skill loads, resolves the source as a commit, and explains the change file by file with the reasoning behind it.
expectations: The source is resolved as a commit
Each changed file is covered with why it changed, not only what changed

baseline_no_skill.notes: Measurement is tracked separately; see evals/README.md.

scenarios.query: Read me evals/fixtures/docs/adr/0007-choose-postgres.md, it's a short decision record.
scenarios.setup: A checkout of this repo at the branch under test, with both skills/ installed, since the scenario tests where the request lands when tts is also available.
scenarios.expected_behavior: The source is already prose, not code or a change. explain-yourself declines the source and the request routes to the tts skill instead, per the last line of explain-yourself's description.
expectations: explain-yourself does not produce a code-style walkthrough of an ADR
No file-by-file change explanation is generated for a document that has no changes
The response either renders the ADR through tts or offers mp3 output, and the run record names which of those two happened

baseline_no_skill.notes: Measurement is tracked separately. Without either skill installed the model has nothing to mis-route to, so this scenario only carries information once both skills are present; the baseline is recorded for symmetry.
